findings.title: Device tagging moved from async goroutine to synchronous request path
findings.body: TagDevice used to run in a background goroutine with its own timeout. It now runs synchronously on every anonymous authentication. When a device limit is set, each uncached request does a COUNT query and then an INSERT or UPDATE against the DB. This adds DB latency to every anonymous request. A slow or failing DB now delays or degrades anonymous auth, even when no limit is configured.

findings.title: Cache set before store write lets rejected devices bypass the limit
findings.body: tagDeviceUI writes the device to localCache before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice. If the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, the cache entry stays in place. For the next 29 minutes, requests from that device hit the cache and return nil. Authentication then succeeds, so the device limit is only enforced on the first request.

findings.title: Count-then-insert race allows exceeding device limit
findings.body: The limit check counts devices and then inserts in a separate statement, with no transaction or lock. Concurrent requests from new devices across goroutines or instances can all see count < limit and all insert. The configured limit can therefore be exceeded.

findings.title: RowsAffected==0 misreported as limit reached on MySQL
findings.body: By default, MySQL reports only changed rows in RowsAffected. When an existing device updates with identical client_ip, user_agent, and updated_at (second precision), 0 rows are reported as affected. ErrDeviceLimitReached is then returned for a device that is already registered, and authentication is denied.

findings.title: Raw error returned on limit with no proper authn error/status
findings.body: When the limit is reached, Authenticate returns a plain error instead of a typed authn/errutil error. The client gets a generic failure with no clear HTTP status or message explaining that the anonymous device limit was reached.
